episodes.191851: A storm rapidly developed in Saskatchewan, turned right and tracked southeastward into Montana.  The storm spawned a couple other storms that would track east-southeast across Montana counties that border Canada.  Funnel clouds, tornadoes and large hail were generated with these storms.
episodes.191860: A surge of upper level tropical moisture pushed into central California from the southeast during the morning of July 13 and continued for much of the day. At first the thunderstorms were mainly dry as the lower and middle levels remained dry, and lightning from these thunderstorms ignited several new wildfires across the area. As the middle levels became more moist during the late afternoon and evening the thunderstorms became more in the way of rain producers. There were some locations in Yosemite National Park and the Upper San Joaquin River Basin which picked up between a quarter and a half inch of rainfall, but lower elevations generally only picked up a trace to a few hundredths of and inch of rain. There were also several reports of hail with one cell in Yosemite National Park.
episodes.191876: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon on Saturday (7/13) as the area reached its convective temperature.  These initial storms produced large hail up to 3 inches, gusty winds, and heavy rainfall across central Wisconsin.  Flash Flooding was reported in Wausau as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell during the afternoon. ||A line of severe thunderstorms, associated with a mesoscale convective vortex, then tracked through central and east-central Wisconsin during the late afternoon and early evening hours on Saturday (7/13).  These storms produced damaging winds, small hail, and heavy rainfall.  Flash Flooding was noted in the Appleton area as 2.5 to 3.5 inches of rain fell during the early evening hours.
episodes.191914: Scattered clusters of storms resulted in large hail over portions of east-central Minnesota during the afternoon on July 13. One storm produced a brief tornado in Rice County. A line of storms then developed over northwestern Minnesota during the evening and travelled southeast across central Minnesota throughout the night. This line led to numerous reports of hail and wind damage before it weakened as it moved into Wisconsin.||An unusually warm and humid air mass resulted in heat index values greater than 100F across portions of southern and western Minnesota during the afternoon and evening of July 13. The combination of several thunderstorms and persistent cloud cover kept heat index values in the low to mid 80s further east.
episodes.191945: A very strong mid level ridge slowly moved through the region, resulting in multiple days of excessive heat. At least one instance of injury and fatality were reported from the heat. The strong ridge eventually shifted far enough east and south of the area to allow sufficient moisture to return, resulting in the development of diurnal convection, with some thunderstorms yielding strong wind gusts.
episodes.191981: A disturbance generated a round of severe storms across the region during the late afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.192050: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon of July 13th producing isolated wind damage.||Scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening of July 13th and continued into the early morning of July 14th producing significant flash flooding in Rockford as well as isolated wind damage.
episodes.192051: Scattered thunderstorms moved across Lake Michigan during the late afternoon and early evening of July 13th.  An outflow boundary raced ahead of the thunderstorms as they slowly dissipated.
episodes.192156: A northwesterly flow aloft combined with ample instability and shear to result in a few supercells across Hill and Blaine counties. Hail was the main severe caliber threat, though there was a wind report.
episodes.192203: Thunderstorms produced strong winds over the southern bay of Green Bay during the evening hours on Saturday (7/13).
episodes.192589: A stalled frontal boundary along the Coastal Plain brought isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms to the coastal waters along the Crystal Coast. A thunderstorm or two become strong in nature and produced damaging wind gusts as it impacted the area on the evening of July 12th.
episodes.193173: A couple strong to severe thunderstorms moved southeast out of the Black Hills area into the northern Nebraska panhandle late in the evening on the 12th.
episodes.193335: Moderate to strong instability combined with sufficient shear and several shortwave troughs created chances for strong to severe storms. Hail, wind gusts, and reported tornadoes occurred.
episodes.193456: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over southern Crook County, producing wind gusts to near 60 mph.
episodes.193458: A severe thunderstorm developed over western Fall River County and tracked southeast into Nebraska. The storm produced large hail in the Edgemont area.
episodes.193459: A severe thunderstorm developed over central Perkins County and tracked eastward. The storm produced large hail and strong wind gusts from southeast of Bison to south of Meadow.
episodes.193526: Scattered thunderstorms moved across east-central Kansas during the early morning hours on both July 12 and 13, producing isolated hail, gusty winds, and flooding.
episodes.193740: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the Pine Ridge of northern Sheridan county during the early evening hours of July 12th. These storms became severe over northeastern Sheridan county where they produced quarter sized hail north of Gordon.
episodes.194083: A couple lines of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across southern WI with reports of damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding. The storms developed along a warm front.
episodes.194183: Thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening hours on July 13th. These initially took on supercell characteristics producing hail both near the Mississippi River and across portions of Dodge County before moving southeast and forming into a line of storms that produced localized wind damage.
episodes.194321: Scattered clusters of storms that developed over Minnesota eventually moved east and reached western Wisconsin. One cell in particular became strong, with thunderstorm wind gusts toppling a tree in Pepin County.
episodes.194387: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on the 12th in the Quad State. Wind damage occurred in the town of Sesser, including tree and powerline damage. Storms from the previous evening in Sesser might have made some trees more susceptible to damage. Meanwhile, torrential rainfall with nearly stationary storms near Tamaroa produced flash flooding. Isolated storms continued overnight as heavy rain and minimal storm motion caused flash flooding issues in Murphysboro and other locations in or near Jackson County, Illinois. Storm total rainfall peaked around 2-3 inches in parts of Jackson and Perry Counties, most of which fell within an hour or two at each respective location. Shear was minimal while SBCAPE reached 2000-3000 J/kg during the afternoon on the 12th, dropping to 1000-2000 J/kg overnight. PW values were near 1.75 inch.
episodes.194388: Early to mid afternoon diurnally driven thunderstorms developed in Southwest Indiana, then progressed eastward. Heavy rainfall rates (PWs around 1.7 inch) produced ponding of water on roads in Evansville, while nickel size hail was also reported. Localized boundaries helped with storm development. MLCAPE was around 2000-2500 J/kg while shear was limited.
episodes.194403: During the afternoon and evening hours on July 13th, storms of various modes moved across portions of western Wisconsin producing both large hail and damaging wind gusts. As storms progressed eastward, they developed into a line and continued to produce wind damage as they moved into central Wisconsin.
episodes.194565: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.194642: Thunderstorms developed initially over western North Dakota during the afternoon and early evening hours before also forming over central North Dakota later in the evening. This as an upper level short wave trough approached the area and a frontal boundary moved in from Montana. The first storm to develop was over Dunn County and quickly produced a tornado. The tornado occurred over an open field south of Manning and impacted no structures. There was no damage to evaluate, therefore it was rated EF-U (Unknown) by NWS policy. Thereafter, the main threat with the thunderstorms was large hail. The largest reported hail was the size of a baseball, and also occurred in Dunn County. There were also reports of severe wind gusts, particularly towards the end of the event with the later storms. With that said, the strongest wind gust did occur during the middle of the event near Plaza, Mountrail County, where estimated 75 mph wind gusts cause tree damage.
episodes.194721: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.194960: Monsoon moisture moving in from the south fueled isolated thunderstorms, a few of which produced high winds. In addition, a wildfire of unknown origin damaged infrastructure on the southeast edge of Kingman.
episodes.194961: Monsoon moisture seeping in from the south fueled isolated thunderstorms, a few of which produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.194962: Monsoon moisture seeping in from the south fueled isolated thunderstorms, a few of which produced high winds.
episodes.194991: Shortwave energy moved through the region during the morning hours of July 13, 2024, bringing showers and thunderstorms along and north of Interstate 44. Severe thunderstorms resulted in 60 mph winds and reports of tree damage in Miller and Camden counties.
episodes.195018: A weak frontal boundary pushed through Maine during the evening hours of July 13th.  A hot unstable airmass was in place with above normal temperatures and deep moisture.  This allowed for a line of scattered thunderstorms to develop in a weak sheer environment.  Most storms were on the strong side, but a severe storm did develop in York and Kennebec County.
episodes.195019: A weak frontal boundary pushed through New Hampshire during the evening hours of July 13th. A hot unstable airmass was in place with above normal temperatures and deep moisture. This allowed for a line of scattered thunderstorms to develop in a weak sheer environment. Most storms were on the strong side, but a severe storm did develop in Carroll County briefly before crossing the state line.
episodes.195087: Monsoon moisture over Arizona allowed thunderstorms to form across the area. One storm produce strong outflow winds that hit Winslow.
episodes.195130: A 61 mph wind gust measured at Lost River Rest Area.
episodes.195215: Scattered thunderstorms developed within a hot and humid air mass along the Ohio River during the afternoon hours on July 13th. While most of the thunderstorms did not produce severe weather in southern Indiana, a downburst over Harrison County produced isolated wind damage as well as sub-severe hail.
episodes.195216: Scattered thunderstorms developed within a hot and humid air mass along the Ohio River during the afternoon hours on July 13th. While most of the thunderstorms did not produce severe weather, isolated wind damage was reported near Goshen in Oldham County.
